subject: SLA negotiation: Veridian Health baseline uptime & monthly remedy alignment
messages:
From: Samantha Green <samantha.green@veridianhealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com; karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@veridianhealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Revisions to Redwood SLA draft - baseline & remedies

Hi Aditya / Karthik,

Thanks for the draft SLA you shared yesterday. We've reviewed and our legal/procurement team pushed back on two points that matter for our internal risk committee: the baseline uptime floor and the monthly remedy calculation.

High level asks from Veridian:
- Baseline uptime: we'd like a guaranteed monthly uptime floor of 99.5% across all hosted routes (we understand some of your customers are on 99.9+, but Veridian needs a stronger baseline).
- Remedy: instead of a flat pro-rata credit tied directly to downtime minutes, we want a soft cap that allows larger monthly credits if outages materially affect scheduled clinical workloads.
- Exception carve-outs: heavy batch workloads for nightly analytics and scheduled maintenance windows should be excluded from the uptime calculation, or at minimum counted under a different band (we proposed 97% for batch-only flows).

I've attached our redlines (Veridian-SLA-Redlines-v1.pdf) and a short note on the clinical tolerance windows. Can you review and let us know what is feasible from Redwood's operations perspective? Also: can you share a small snapshot of p95 latency for the last 30 days for our pilot routes (we need it for our SOC/operational review)?

Tom (copied) will be the primary procurement owner on our side for final sign-off.

Best,
Samantha Green
Director, Vendor Risk & Procurement
Veridian Health

Attachment: Veridian-SLA-Redlines-v1.pdf

From: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-12-01T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Revisions to Redwood SLA draft - baseline & remedies

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear redlines and context. We appreciate how important this is for Veridian's clinical SLAs. I pulled together an operationally realistic counter-proposal and attached a brief metrics CSV for the pilot routes (service-metrics-snapshot.csv).

Summary of Redwood's proposed compromise:
- Baseline uptime: Redwood can commit to a 99.75% monthly uptime floor for interactive (real-time API) routes.
- Batch/analytics flows: these will be treated under a separate band with a 97.0% monthly floor; batch will be eligible for a different remedy ladder.
- Monthly remedy: credits will be tiered (see table in attached line-item):
  * 99.75% - 99.0% => 5% monthly usage credit
  * 99.0% - 97.5% => 15% monthly usage credit
  * <97.5% => 30% monthly usage credit, with an additional discretionary remediation for documented production impact up to 50% in exceptional cases (requires escalation and verification)
- Caps & exclusions: total monthly credits capped at 100% of the month's Redwood invoice for the affected service. Scheduled maintenance (with >48h notice) and customer-triggered load (e.g., deliberate bulk ingestion exceeding agreed QPS) will be excluded from uptime calculation provided we can demonstrate normal operating patterns.
- Latency SLO: for interactive routes we propose p95 < 250ms; if Veridian needs tighter latency, we can offer a higher-commitment route (different pricing / dedicated pool).

Operational notes:
- The batch carve-out is important because the nightly analytics job you described can cause sustained high GPU utilization and queueing; if that remains in the uptime band you'll see spiky behavior and a higher credit exposure that makes the pricing unsustainable.
- For the discretionary remediation above 30%, we will require a joint incident report and a 3rd-party verification window (standard for enterprise escalations).

Next steps I propose:
1) Laura and I will run those redlines against our standard contract language and send a marked-up SLA term sheet.
2) We will provision a 30-day pilot with the 99.75/97.0 bands and deliver the p95/p99 latency reports weekly.
3) Karthik will coordinate a short exec call this week to align on legal/ops.

Attached: service-metrics-snapshot.csv (30-day p95/p99, uptime per-route)

Happy to hop on a call — propose Thurs 12/3 10:00 AM PT.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: service-metrics-snapshot.csv

From: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-12-01T15:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Revisions to Redwood SLA draft - baseline & remedies

Samantha,

Thanks for sending the redlines. A couple of legal items I want to call out explicitly so procurement has clarity:

1) Baseline definitions: We can accept different uptime bands for interactive vs batch, but we need the definitions in the SLA to be instrumented by route labels and explicit traffic gating rules. Ambiguity around what constitutes "batch" will cause disputes.
2) Remedy mechanics: We are comfortable with a tiered credit ladder, but we must limit (a) total monthly credits to 100% of the affected service invoice and (b) root-cause escalation windows for discretionary extra credits.
3) Force majeure & scheduled maintenance: Redwood requires a 48-hour scheduled maintenance notice plus a 4 hour emergency maintenance carve-out for critical security patches.
4) Auditability: Veridian requested broader audit rights in the redlines — we can offer operational logs and aggregated metrics but not raw production telemetry; any additional audit scope will need an addendum.

I'll turn this into a marked-up SLA term-sheet and share by end of day tomorrow. Aditya/Karthik: please confirm if the 99.75/97.0 split is acceptable commercially; we may need to make it 99.7 to align with internal reporting thresholds.

Best,
Laura Bennett
VP, Legal — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
To: Samantha Green <samantha.green@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@veridianhealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:46:00-08:00
Subject: Quick alignment and proposed next steps (call invite)

Samantha / Tom — following up to lock the operational next steps so procurement can progress:

- Proposed commercial: 99.75% interactive floor / 97.0% batch floor. This is the package we can set on the pilot pricing.
- Pilot: 30 days from go-live, Redwood will deliver weekly p95/p99 and uptime reports.
- Escalation: For anything that would trigger >30% remedy, we'll need an incident review and joint validation.

I've created a short agenda and shared a tentative 30-minute call slot on Thurs 12/3 at 10:00 AM PT (invite sent). Please confirm and we'll include a short deck with sample monthly credit calculations and examples of scheduled maintenance notices.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com

From: Samantha Green <samantha.green@veridianhealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@veridianhealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T16:41:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Revisions to Redwood SLA draft - baseline & remedies

Aditya / Laura / Karthik — thanks for the fast turnaround and for the proposed compromise. Veridian is prepared to proceed on the pilot with the following confirmations:

1) Accept the 99.75% interactive / 97.0% batch floors for the 30-day pilot.
2) Agreed on the tiered credit ladder described in Aditya's note, subject to the 100% monthly invoice cap.
3) Veridian will label the nightly analytics routes explicitly as "batch" in our routing rules so the bands are unambiguous.
4) We accept the scheduled maintenance carve-out with the 48-hour notice; please ensure the maintenance notice template is included in the final SLA document.

For the exec call tomorrow, can you include 1 slide that shows: (a) sample credit calc for a 6-hour partial outage and (b) the steps & timeline for discretionary remediation? Also confirm that the metrics CSV you attached includes the pilot routes only.

Tom and I will sign-off on pilot commencement once we receive the marked-up SLA term-sheet from Laura.

Thanks again — look forward to the call.

Best,
Samantha Green
Director, Vendor Risk & Procurement
Veridian Health

P.S. Attachment verified: Veridian-SLA-Redlines-v1.pdf (we'll upload a signed copy after the pilot agreement).
